{
  "research_question": "Does mouse navigation performance differ across五种 stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Despite right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81), the large sample size (n=76,655) provides robustness to moderate violations; consider log-transformation or Welch's ANOVA if variance heterogeneity is severe.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1) with mean 0.73; standard ANOVA is inappropriate. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or chi-square test of independence, to assess differential success rates across paradigms.",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Extreme right skew (max=29.82) and low minimum (0.000928) suggest severe heteroscedasticity; consider rank-based ANOVA (Kruskal-Wallis) or gamma GLM with log link as superior alternatives.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Moderate right skew (max=75.35) but bounded positive support; check variance homogeneity and consider Welch's ANOVA or robust methods if needed.",
    "AD (angular dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Bounded [0,1] with mean 0.38; arcsine or logit transformation may improve variance stabilization, or use beta regression for proper bounded support."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence:-verify no serial correlation within mouse sessions; the 8 mice with repeated measures structure may violate independence. Random effects for Mouse or mixed-effects model may be required.",
    "Normality: assess via Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk on residuals; given n=76,655, formal tests will reject but visual inspection and effect size robustness matter more.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test for each continuous variable; expected violations for Path Efficiency and possibly Time-to-Target given extreme maxima.",
    "Sample size imbalance: Combined has 48,846 trials vs Bright Visual Only with 3,323; Welch's ANOVA or weighted methods address this.",
    "Binary outcome handling: Success requires explicit binomial modeling, not Gaussian approximation."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous responses with significant omnibus F-test: pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD for balanced variance, or Games-Howell for unequal variances/sample sizes.",
    "Specific contrasts of interest: Combined vs all unimodal conditions; ICMS Only vs Visual conditions; Dim vs Bright Visual; all active vs Sham.",
    "For Success (logistic model): estimated marginal means with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons on log-odds scale, transformed to probability differences.",
    "Effect size reporting: eta-squared or partial eta-squared for ANOVA; odds ratios for Success; Cliff's delta or rank-biserial for non-parametric alternatives.",
    "Multiplicity control: Family-wise error rate at alpha=0.05 across 5×10=50 planned comparisons suggests conservative Bonferroni or false discovery rate control."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined paradigm likely shows fastest Time-to-Target and highest Success given largest sample size and putative multimodal facilitation, but effect size magnitude uncertain without variance decomposition.",
    "Sham condition expected to show poorest performance (higher Time-to-Target, lower Success, lower Path Efficiency) serving as baseline.",
    "ICMS Only vs Visual Only comparison tests sensory substitution equivalence; directional prediction uncertain without prior mechanistic hypotheses.",
    "Dim vs Bright Visual may reveal luminance-dependent performance differences in path integration.",
    "Path Efficiency and AD expected to be negatively correlated: higher angular dispersion predicts lower path efficiency across paradigms."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in Stim Paradigm frequencies (Combined 63.7% of data vs Bright Visual Only 4.3%) reduces power for rare-condition comparisons and complicates variance estimation.",
    "Repeated measures structure (8 mice, multiple trials each) ignored in standard ANOVA inflates Type I error; Mouse as random effect essential for valid inference.",
    "Extreme outliers in Path Efficiency (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47) and Time-to-Target (max=201.4) suggest data quality issues or multi-modal distributions that ANOVA handles poorly.",
    "Missing covariates: no trial number, session day, or learning effects captured; performance may change with experience, confounding paradigm comparisons.",
    "Summary_only data view precludes trial-level sequence analysis, trajectory reconstruction, and temporal dynamics assessment."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit mixed-effects models with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect for continuous outcomes, using appropriate distributions (log-normal for Time-to-Target, gamma for Path Efficiency, beta for AD, binomial for Success). Estimate paradigm differences with likelihood ratio tests and profile confidence intervals. If computational constraints prohibit mixed models, aggregate to mouse-level means and apply standard ANOVA on n=8 mice with paradigm as within-subject factor, accepting reduced power but valid inference."
}
